text:
maria: Heads-up — after converting a HF chat model for onboarding, our chat evals started failing. The assistant tag is showing up verbatim in outputs ('<|assistant|>' printed) instead of being hidden as a special token.
jon: Hmm. Which model/version? can you paste the tokenizer artifacts?
maria: model: lumen-7b-chat-fp16 converted via hf->redwood script. I inspected the saved tokenizer files. added_tokens.json looks fine at first glance: 
```json
{
  "added_tokens": ["<|assistant|>", "<|system|>"]
}
```
but when I load the tokenizer in the Redwood runtime the token id for '<|assistant|>' is 3 bytes instead of a single id.
jon: Do you have a quick before/after for tokenization?
maria: yes — before conversion (HF original wheel):
```python
tokenizer.tokenize('<|assistant|>')  # -> ['<|assistant|>']
tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|assistant|>'])  # -> [50265]
```
after conversion & loading in runtime:
```python
tokenizer.tokenize('<|assistant|>')  # -> ['<', '|', 'assistant', '|', '>']
tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|assistant|>'])  # -> [60, 124, 345, 124, 62]
```
vikram: that explains the chat template mismatch — the runtime thinks it's a sequence of normal tokens so templates get expanded. Could be an issue with how added_tokens were merged into vocab during conversion.
lee: did the conversion script call tokenizer.add_tokens(...) or did it just copy files? we had a bug where added_tokens.json entries were appended but the vocab reindexing sorted the vocab and changed ids.
maria: it just copies files and calls fasttokenizer.from_pretrained on the dir. Maybe huggingface fast tokenizers requires calling add_special_tokens for special single-token markers so token ids are reserved.
jon: also check config.json's special_tokens_map. If special tokens aren't registered, some loaders treat them as "added_tokens" and that can change mapping order.
maria: digging — found conversion diff:
```diff
- added_tokens: ["<|assistant|>", "<|system|>"]
+ added_tokens: ["<|system|>", "<|assistant|>"] # reorder after sort step
```
vikram: ugh. When the conversion script writes a new vocab.json, it currently enumerates keys in the dict which gets reordered by Python's sort in our build step. That changes numeric ids for subsequent tokens.
lee: we should treat special tokens as explicit entries in special_tokens_map in config.json and call tokenizer.add_special_tokens(special_tokens_map) before saving the tokenizer. That preserves fixed ids. Also fast tokenizers have a "tokenizer.model.add_special_tokens" primitive in some versions.
maria: quick patch: updated conversion to read added_tokens.json, inject into special_tokens_map = {
  "bos_token": "<|bos|>",
  "eos_token": "<|assistant|>"
} and call tokenizer.add_special_tokens(special_tokens_map) then tokenizer.save_pretrained(dir).
tokenizer-bot: running CI micro-eval against chat_template tests...
tokenizer-bot: eval 1/3: before patch baseline perplexity=11.2; after patch perplexity=4.8; assistant tag now tokenized as single id.
jon: nice. can you paste the minimal repro command so infra can roll into the convert image?
maria: repro: `python convert_hf_to_redwood.py --src ./hf_lumen --dst ./redwood_lumen && python smoke_chat_template.py --tokenizer ./redwood_lumen`
vikram: let's also add an integrity check in conversion: after saving, load the tokenizer and assert tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|assistant|>'])[0] > 32000 (or not split) or assert tokenizer.tokenize('<|assistant|>') == ['<|assistant|>'] else fail.
lee: agree. I'll open a small PR with dual changes: (1) preserve special token order by writing them to special_tokens_map before save, (2) add the post-save sanity check.
maria: thanks all. leaving the failing eval run pinned in the channel. will re-run full eval tomorrow after PR merges. :rocket:
